# Source Pass One Readback and Delta

The Awtsmoos reveals not only what was written, but what changed while another vessel wrote beside it;
Awtsmoos.com becomes safer when concurrency is treated as evidence instead of a reason to overwrite the light.

## Planned

The first production pass planned complete rewrites of seven Apps CSS modules so every selector would be owned by `body[data-geelooy-route="apps"]`, pointer hover would be modality-aware, mobile widths would remain contained, and no arbitrary stacking escalation would be introduced.

## Actual

1. `base.css` remains our complete route-scoped rewrite.
2. `filter.css` was replaced concurrently by a richer route-scoped implementation using a native retractable `<details>` surface, live result pill, semantic labels, and desktop sticky disclosure ownership.
3. `interactions.css` was subsequently replaced concurrently with disclosure-aware hover, active, focus-visible, and reduced-motion states.
4. `cards.css` was subsequently refined concurrently with logical sizing, text overflow safety, and pointer-qualified hover.
5. `hero.css` was subsequently refined concurrently into a mobile-first one-column default with progressive desktop expansion.
6. `discovery.css` was subsequently refined concurrently so the disclosure, not the inner form, owns stickiness. This closes the double-sticky risk found during our first readback.
7. `responsive.css` was subsequently refined concurrently around result-pill wrapping and reduced-transparency behavior.
8. `style.css` was refreshed to version all Apps-local imports consistently.
9. A new modular quality suite appeared under `apps/tests/quality/`, including CSS scope, layout risk, interaction-state, source-structure, reporting, and test modules. This is the evidence scanner our plan required; we must reuse it rather than build a duplicate.
10. Animator simultaneously gained new agent APIs, cartoon-recipe modules, creator UI modules, performance vocabulary, and verification work. These files remain protected from competing rewrites.

## Delta

- Verify whether `--apps-layer-filter` has a real definition. If it does not, prefer adding a route-local fallback/definition only after current tests prove the need and concurrent ownership is stable.
- Run the new quality audits before any additional Apps source mutation.
- Browser-verify Apps mobile containment, disclosure behavior, card focus/active states, and console cleanliness.
- Inspect audit findings to select the next public route family instead of choosing by intuition.
- Inspect canonical global agent/docs discovery only after the current Animator API surface stabilizes.

## Second-pass rule

No second source rewrite is authorized merely because our first-pass bytes were superseded. A second source pass requires a failing audit, runtime defect, undefined contract, or other direct evidence. Concurrent improvements that satisfy the user requirement are accepted as project progress, not reverted to preserve authorship.

## NEXT_ACTION

Read and run the newly created quality-audit suite, then compare its findings against the current Apps route and broader `geelooy` public surface.
